title: Cold & Flu Relief

drivers.name: Price increase (6.2%)
drivers.evidence: Two recent weeks at $12.03 show 1.15x and 1.26x baseline. Historical data shows price increases reduce demand. Noise-adjusted effect of similar price hikes is negative. Supplier note adds supply risk.

drivers.name: Supplier delivery warning
drivers.evidence: Planner note indicates potential delivery shortfall. This could reduce in-stock availability and suppress sales. Noted as a risk driver.

adjustment.analysis: Baseline median is 19.0. No event or promotion in target week. Price increased 6.2% to $12.03. Recent weeks at $12.03 show elevated sales: 24 units (1.26x baseline) on 2026-10-05, 13 units (1.15x) on 2026-09-28. The average uplift at this price is 1.21x baseline (13.5 vs 11.33). Supplier delivery warning adds downside risk. Past promotions at similar discount levels show noise-adjusted lift of x1.4, but this is a price increase, not a promotion. Price hike likely suppresses demand. Combine evidence: moderate downside from price and supply risk. Adjust median down, widen spreads for uncertainty.

brief:
PRODUCT: Cold & Flu Relief | category Health | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-18 (next week)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 12.03 (+6.2% vs regular price 11.33)
  planner notes: Supplier warns of a short delivery

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 19.0 | 5%-95%: 7.2 - 34.4 | 10%-90%: 10.3 - 30.9

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-46% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
